definitions.gloss: busyness; being extremely busy; peak period of work
definitions.explanation: A somewhat formal term describing a state of being very busy, often used in business contexts to refer to peak seasons or hectic periods.

examples.japanese: {繁忙期|はんぼうき}に{入|はい}った。
{年末|ねんまつ}は{繁忙|はんぼう}を{極|きわ}める。
examples.english: The end of the year is extremely hectic.

examples.japanese: {繁忙期|はんぼうき}には{残業|ざんぎょう}が{増|ふ}えるので{体調|たいちょう}{管理|かんり}に{気|き}をつけている。
examples.english: During the busy season, overtime increases, so I take care to manage my health.

notes:
A formal word for extreme busyness, most commonly encountered in the compound {繁忙期|はんぼうき} (busy season/period). Composed of {繁|はん} (flourishing, thriving) + {忙|ぼう} (busy). The word carries a business or organizational tone and is rarely used in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {繁忙期|はんぼうき}: busy season, peak period
- {繁忙|はんぼう}を{極|きわ}める: to be extremely busy
- {繁忙|はんぼう}{状態|じょうたい}: state of being very busy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {多忙|たぼう}: very busy — similar in formality; focuses on having too much to do
- {忙|いそが}しい: busy — the everyday adjective for being busy
- {閑散|かんさん}: quiet, slack — the opposite; a period of low activity
- {繁盛|はんじょう}: thriving, prosperous — describes a business doing well, not just being busy
